recipes.name: Honey and Rosemary Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 3 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cut in 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment paper.

Mix olive oil, honey, rosemary, salt, and black pepper together in a large bowl, and stir sweet potato cubes in the mixture to coat. Remove sweet potato cubes with a slotted spoon, and arrange them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until tender, about 45 minutes. Turn the oven heat up to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and bake until browned, another 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey and Rosemary Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These rosemary sweet potatoes are a simple, savory-sweet delight that is roasted in the oven with honey, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Very addictive!

review.reviewBody: Very easy and sooo delicious. The carmelized glaze started to stick as they started to cool when removing from the foil lining, so I just put the pan back in the oven to re-warm and they came off fine!

To the reviewers who said the potatoes got burnt: it's not because of the honey, but because the recipe calls for olive oil. This is a mistake. The burning point for olive oil is low. Use either canola oil or walnut oil. 

Pour the honey into a bowl and mix in the 2 T oil, then add the rosemary and 1/2 tsp salt along with 1/4 tsp of pepper (less than the recipe calls for). I cubed the sweet potatoes, tossed them in a bowl with the sauce, threw them in a parchment-lined 9 x 13 ceramic pan, and baked at 400 for 45 minutes, stirring them after 20 mns.

Turned out really good, with a bit of a glaze.

I've made this several times and brought to parties/BBQs and it is always a hit. I stopped peeling the potatoes, no need. Just chop, mix everything really well in a plastic bag. 
Set up a baking sheet with parchment paper, spread out the potatoes flat, bake and perfection. Then I toss in a chafing pan cover for transportation and reheating as needed when I get to my final destination. Or put in a covered dish for home serving.

Much less baking time is needed. Cook for 20-25 minutes and turn up the heat for 10-15 minutes. Otherwise perfect as is! I do think it's really important to use fresh rosemary. There is one other thing I did by accident. I don't actually know if it made a difference. Mine weren't sticky at all, but they were sweet, so maybe this is the trick if you're having trouble with overly sticky yams. I put together the ingredients about 3-4 hours ahead of time and left them out of the fridge and although the sauce was very thick when i first put it together, it was very liquidy when it was time to make them. I followed the directions and removed them from the liquid with a slotted spoon, then strained out the rosemary from the liquid, tossed the rosemary with the yams. These were the highlight of our thanksgiving meal!

I made this for our Thanksgiving dinner today. Everyone loved it, but two people thought the rosemary was too strong. What I will do next time is lay a couple of whole sprigs across the top and later remove them before serving. That way I can infuse the potatoes with the flavor, but more subtlety.

Made this for a family gathering & everyone loved it! Even the kids. I modified by adding a tablespoon of bourbon & mixed all ingredients in a small shaker before adding to diced sweet potatoes. As our family says “it’s a keeper “.

Great recipe. Made in quantity for a church dinner so a bit labor intensive but especially popular with the vegans in the crowd. One hint- I microwaved 5 large sweet potatoes for 1 minute - then cut in 1/2” slices. (Softens them just enough to ease slicing). Then I tossed with rosemary etc in plastic bag. Baked 30 minutes at 350. When slightly cooled I took a sharp knife and took off the skin. Worked great. Easier than peeling. Reheated on low oven to serve. 35 large potatoes fed 75 people with s bit to spare.

I really liked these, but my husband said "too sweet". Taking the potatoes out of the mixing bowl with the slotted spoon and allowing the sauce to drain is important in order to avoid burning. I forgot and just dumped the mixture onto the pan. Where there was extra sauce it started to burn so I had to take them out early, but they were still delicious.
Absolutely loved these! I steamed the potatoes a bit first to speed up cooking time. Yummy. Oh I used yams too
I microwaved the potatoes the potatoes to save tme. These were awesome

Woah Nellie these are tasty! Use parchment instead of foil and there will be no sticking. These smell amazing when they're cooking! Everyone gobbled these up. I used about half the amount of rosemary to be safe (it can be overpowering), but next time I'll use the full amount. I also used half the amount of black pepper. This one's a keeper!
Fantastic recipe. Healthy and addictive. A pure contradiction in terms!
This was very easy to make and a family hit! Will make again!
This is one of the easiest and tastiest yam recipes I’ve made yet!! I will definitely make again!
This was so easy and my guests loved it. This is a new staple for our household.
Excellent, very good flavor from the rosemary.

Making this for the 2nd time. This time I'm using canola oil, a little less rosemary than I used last time which I used more than 2 tbs last time. I decided to use brown sugar and cherrywood smoked salt.
This has become a favorite at Thanksgiving! Nice alternative to the traditional sweet potato casserole.
